HOME SCIENCE MARCH — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Convenience Foods? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Convenience Foods.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Convenience Foods.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Convenience Foods.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Special Treatment in Laundry Work? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting.

13. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.

   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

17. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

20. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)

22. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts
